# Frutiger Aero

A Frutiger Aero skin for the DSH Web GUI: ice-blue translucent glass panels over an original sky-and-grass wallpaper, with slowly rising glossy bubbles.

## Highlights

- **Original procedural artwork** — the background (`assets/aero-sky.webp`) is fully generated by code (sky gradient, sun, clouds, grass field). No third-party images. MIT licensed.
- **Light bubbles** — 6 per 500px tile, single-layer radial gradients, floating on a `transform` compositor animation: no repaints, no layer promotion, no animated background positions.
- **Full token remap** — every `--dsw-alias-*` and `--aion-*` token is remapped to the cold ice-blue palette; light and dark variants are both complete.
- **Readability budgeted** — text colors are chosen against the composite glass background; body and secondary text meet WCAG AA.

## Design language

| Role | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canvas | `#CDE8FA` | `#081a2e` |
| Glass panels | white at ~22% of the background-opacity scrim | navy at ~20% + scrim |
| Text | `#0B2540` | `#DCEBFA` |
| Accent | `#3FB8E8` | `#5AC8F5` |

Bubbles: 6 per 500px tile, fixed pixel radii (44–92px), single-layer gradients, rising at 25px/s. The animation translates exactly one tile per cycle, and the layer extends one tile beyond the viewport bottom, so the field covers the screen at every instant and loops seamlessly. Circles are kept fully inside their tile so the tile boundary never clips them.

## Frosted glass and performance

Frost is applied through the structural regions' real CSS-Module class names
(matched with `[class*=]`, since the hash prefix changes between builds):

| Region | Selector | Radius |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Left workspace column | `[class*="sidebarCol"]` | none (clear glass) |
| Centre chat column | `[class*="centerCol"]` | 2px |
| Right workspace column | `[class*="rightbarCol"]` | 3px |
| Top titlebar strip | `[class*="_frame"]::before` | 2px |

Visible seams come from neighbouring regions carrying *different* blur radii, so
the spread is kept as small as possible (3px at most in the table above) and none
of the three seams reads as a step.

The left workspace column carries no frost: it contains the sidebar's
collapse/expand button, and `backdrop-filter` makes an element a containing block
for its descendants, which would re-base that absolutely positioned button from
the window onto the sidebar column — dropping it onto the sidebar heading when
expanded, and clipping it away behind `overflow:hidden` when collapsed. The
column therefore uses clear glass, and the material difference is expressed
through the `--dsw-specific-sidebar-fill` alpha instead.

On an Intel Iris Xe iGPU, with the animated bubble field running behind all of
these surfaces, GPU 3D engine utilisation stays **below 0.3%**.

The one expensive pattern is a window-level blur: `backdrop-filter: blur(16px)`
on the huge `[data-dsh-part="dialog"]` layer costs roughly **+22%** GPU. That
declaration is deliberately absent.

### Glass edges

The window is treated as a single sheet of glass:

- one highlight on the **top edge of the window** (1px line + ~12px soft decay)
- one on the **leftmost edge** (the sidebar's left side, 15%)
- internal seams carry only a **6% soft light** — enough to hint at the
  partitions without forming a bright line
- **no per-panel borders and no per-panel drop shadows**: a real `border` changes
  layout (the shell's elements are not all `border-box`), and a per-panel edge
  highlight adds a bright line exactly at the seams

### Overlay sidebar in narrow windows (viewport < 1024px)

Below 1024px the sidebar becomes a narrow rail; expanding it manually turns it
into an overlay stacked on the squeezed centre column. In that state the sidebar
must be opaque, or the content behind it shows through and the two text layers
overprint — which is why the official default for
`--dsw-specific-sidebar-fill` is an opaque static colour.

This skin gives the column its own near-opaque pane (plus a drop shadow) at the
same breakpoint, while keeping translucent glass in wide windows.

> That token is also the background of the whole frame, so do not override it
> inside the breakpoint — doing so hides the wallpaper as well.

## Attribution

The bubbles' radial alpha profile references
[khang-nd/bubbles](https://github.com/khang-nd/bubbles) (MIT), a recreation of
the Windows Bubbles screensaver. No assets were copied; only the profile values
were used. The wallpaper and all skin code are original.
